notes: PCB layers/sizes/placements are engineering judgement unless 'basis' is a URL; only the ECM/DCU placement count (~412 components, Bosch DCU17HD01 teardown) is sourced.

Sources were read from web-search result snippets; vendor sites could not be fetched (egress blocked) and the search budget ran out before cluster/IVI, NOx/DCU, glow-plug and fuel-pump sources were found - those ICs are engineering judgement.
MHEV/HEV/PHEV semiconductor content is interpolated; Infineon (Dec 2024) publishes ICE ~USD 750 and BEV ~USD 1,300 only.
ADAS boards (2026-10-09): No source found gives a numeric board cost or an RF-laminate £/m² premium; Yole/System Plus/TechInsights/R&M reports that hold them are paywalled.

ADAS boards (2026-10-09): No source gives a layer count, HDI build, board size or surface finish for a production ADAS board; those fields are engineering judgement or 'not published'. Size figures given are reference designs (TI, OmniVision) or a housing (ZF ProAI).
ADAS boards (2026-10-09): No source gives a component placement count for any ADAS board; every placement range is engineering judgement or 'not found'.

ADAS boards (2026-10-09): Bosch MPC3 IC list (R-Car V3H, 32-bit MCU, Samsung RAM, AR0233AT) belongs to the unit TechInsights tore down, Bosch part L8B2-14F404 from a 2020–21 Land Rover Defender. TechInsights calls it a night-vision module projecting a 'thermal' image; AR0233AT is a visible-light HDR CMOS sensor, so 'thermal' is loose wording. eeNews names the V3H as MPC3's central chip, so the IC list matches the MPC3 front camera; the night-vision role is TechInsights' description only.
ADAS boards (2026-10-09): Tesla HW4 memory: 42how says 16 × 2 GB GDDR6; SemiAnalysis / Not a Tesla App say 16 GB per SoC — unresolved.
ADAS boards (2026-10-09): TechInsights' Hesai AT128 summary gives both 128 receivers and '32 laser transmitters and receivers' — inconsistent.
ADAS boards (2026-10-09): Arbe channel split: 2 Tx RFICs × 24 + 4 Rx RFICs × 12 in early descriptions = 48 Tx / 48 Rx; not a teardown.
ADAS boards (2026-10-09): Park-assist ECU: no teardown found; its MCU and board are unknown.
ADAS boards (2026-10-09): Laminate claims from Rogers, Panasonic, Isola, Huber+Suhner and Infineon are supplier statements, not teardown findings.

boardCostEvidence.claim: TechInsights: Tesla HW4 is priced 3× HW3 but its manufacturing cost rose only ~32%.
Electrek, citing an EE Times teardown: Tesla HW3 hardware about $190 a unit (parts only; Electrek doubts it).
Yole (System Plus): Tesla's two FSD SoCs give 21× the performance at 0.8× the manufacturing cost (baseline not stated).
Yole: Desay SV IPU04 with two Orin SoCs is twice as expensive as the one-SoC design.
TI: replacing microvias with through vias saved ~40% of radar PCB cost with negligible area increase; Isola FR408HR antenna layer gives acceptable results at practical ranges.

Radar RF board costly; hybrid PTFE/FR4 asymmetric with planar antenna hard to produce; ~80% of radar substrate is Rogers RO3003 (Japanese makers use Panasonic R-5515) — reseller listing of a 12-radar study.
Autoliv 77 GHz radar teardown report includes an estimate of PCB cost (figure not public).
Rogers RO4830 Plus (2025): woven-glass-free thermoset for cost-sensitive corner radar; lowers PCB cost via fabrication yield, FR-4-style processing.
Hybrid builds (FR4 + RF-optimised laminate) lower system cost v all-RF; RF laminates' high CTE risks delamination.
TI: RO3003 gives lower loss and phase repeatability; RO4835 LoPro better manufacturing yield; AWR1642 EVM uses RO4835 + FR4 hybrid.
Huber+Suhner 3D waveguide antenna removes the need for an RF substrate, making standard PCB materials feasible.
Infineon RASIC cascades at low frequencies, reducing the need for expensive RF materials on the board.
Panasonic R-5515X (thermoset, non-PTFE): -1.4 dB/inch at 77 GHz v -1.8 for a competing PTFE; Dk 3.06, Df 0.0021 @14 GHz.
RO3003G2: Dk 3.07 at 77 GHz, 1.3 dB/inch (5 mil).
Patent: waveguide antenna lets the radar PCB use standard inexpensive FR4.
